A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LieRE research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. All 17 pages were compared; the appendix text and rendered appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: v4 reports original image classification, video classification, and synthetic spatial reasoning results, together with ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–10 and the experimental figures, including the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 4, the LieRE pseudocode in Figure 3, and Appendix C retain the same learned skew-symmetric bases, matrix exponential, and key/query rotations. Block sizes and parameter-sharing options are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, UCF101, and the synthetic Y-and-arrow task. Resolution variation, reduced-data evaluation, and patch-shuffling scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Absolute positional encodings, VisionLlama RoPE, and RoPE-Mixed remain in the corresponding comparisons. Figure 7 still compares LieRE64 with RoPE-Mixed. Removing the ViViT citation does not remove the corresponding video baseline.

E3.justification: The model configurations, synthetic training counts and extended absolute-encoding control, 200-epoch benchmark training, and 30-epoch resolution fine-tuning remain unchanged. Appendix B retains the same preprocessing and hyperparameters; rewritten descriptions do not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: The same data-efficiency, model-size, block-size, parameter-sharing, initialization-sensitivity, shuffling, resolution, compute-efficiency, and attention-map analyses remain. No distinct analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 5 newly specifies bootstrap confidence-interval estimation with B=1000 and alpha=0.05. v4 already reports bootstrapped 95% intervals in Table 6 and statistical tests elsewhere. This adds estimation details without establishing additional training runs or changed uncertainty values.

E6.justification: Tabulated and plotted numerical results are unchanged. However, Section 5.2 removes v4's explicit observation that absolute-encoding variants showed no performance improvement during training on 800,000 examples, while retaining the general convergence statement.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix A proof are unchanged. Section 7's new summary of equivalence to RoPE with learnable phases for 1D inputs restates the existing proof rather than adding theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion now explicitly describe encoding both relative and absolute positions and emphasize controlling positional capacity. Numerical headline gains and the concluding unified-multimodal-architecture prospect are dropped, while the central method and performance contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 interprets shuffling degradation as greater positional reliance rather than greater capability. Section 5.4 suggests a capacity-versus-regularization explanation for the 8-by-8 optimum, and Section 7 adds dependence on matrix-exponential accuracy and numerical stability.

D1.justification: The abstract newly states that checkpoints, as well as code, are publicly available. It removes the four-A100/30-minute CIFAR reproducibility statement. Appendix B's hardware and hyperparameters and Appendix C's implementation remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The Arnab et al. (2021) ViViT citation and bibliography entry are removed. Yoshioka (2024) formalizes the repository reference already supplied as a footnote in v4. Section 2's broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, experimental overview, substantial portions of Sections 5.1 and 5.4, conclusion, and limitations are extensively rewritten. Several subsection headings become more descriptive, and experimental paragraphs are reorganized. This constitutes substantial editorial revision despite stable methods and appendices.

P2.justification: Table 4 moves between columns on page 7, and Table 5 moves from page 8 to page 7, with accompanying text and figure reflow. The same figures and tables retain their designs and content; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: Specifying the bootstrap resampling count improves statistical transparency, while the revised shuffling interpretation and matrix-exponential limitation improve calibration. These are useful refinements to unchanged methods, numerical evidence, and proofs. The removed convergence qualifier and some awkward new wording are limited drawbacks, leaving a modest overall quality improvement.
